content.text:
The document contains a full indemnity architecture. Assessment against the checklists:

**Vendor side (§10(a), p0047–p0051):** Kubient must "indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer" against all third-party Claims arising out of (i) the Services, (ii) the Auction Platform, (iv) breach of any representation or warranty, and (v) Kubient's (and its subcontractors') acts or omissions. Because §9(b)(i) warrants the Service and deliverables are non-infringing, §9(b)(iii) warrants data security, and §9(b)(v)/(ix) warrant compliance with Law, the indemnity reaches third-party IP infringement, Vendor data breach, Vendor breach of law, and Vendor negligence/misconduct — broader than either checklist level, with no exclusions for modifications/combinations/specifications and **no super-cap** (§7(a) even carves indemnification out of the consequential-damages waiver). The absent procure/modify/replace/refund remedy ladder and absent 3× cap are Vendor-side protections whose omission favours us.

**Procedures (§11):** notice, control of defence, and reasonable cooperation are all present.

**Only gap vs. preferred:** affiliates are not named as indemnitees, and Customer's §10(b) indemnity is broader than "Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law." The fallback checklist contains no Customer-indemnity element, so this is a shortfall against preferred wording only — noted, not redlined.

input.quote: (a) Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees from all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs (including, without limitation, reasonable attorneys' fees) or liabilities ("Claims") arising out of or in connection with:
input.rationale: Section 10(a) gives us an express Vendor duty to defend, indemnify and hold harmless AP against all third-party Claims arising out of the Services, the Auction Platform, Kubient's breach of any representation or warranty, and the acts or omissions of Kubient and its subcontractors. Read with the §9(b) warranties — non-infringement of the Service and deliverables (9(b)(i)), data security (9(b)(iii)), and compliance with applicable Laws (9(b)(v), (ix)) — the indemnity captures third-party IP infringement, Vendor-caused data breach, Vendor breach of law, and Vendor negligence/misconduct. Section 11 supplies the standard procedure: prompt written notice (with no forfeiture for delay), indemnitor control of defence and settlement subject to our consent to any liability admission, and reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's cost. This exceeds the fallback: the IP indemnity carries none of the permitted Customer modification/combination/specification exclusions, and there is no 3x annual fees super-cap anywhere in the Agreement — indeed §7(a) carves indemnification liability out of the consequential-damages waiver, so Kubient's exposure is uncapped in our favour. The fallback procure/modify/replace/refund remedy ladder is absent, but that ladder and the super-cap are Vendor-side protections whose omission benefits us and does not weaken our recovery. Two points fall short of preferred wording only and are noted rather than redlined: affiliates are not named among the indemnitees (officers, directors, managers, members, agents and employees are), and our §10(b) indemnity is broader than "Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law" — it also covers unauthorised use of the Services/Platform, breach of our warranties, and our acts or omissions. The fallback checklist contains no Customer-indemnity element, so the bargain is met on its material terms and we would not reopen a favourable, uncapped Vendor indemnity to chase that wording.
